messages.author: f769d7d2cfcf4edc
messages.subject: rstan Suggestion (Tip?): Cancelling mcmc
parts:
Maybe I am just doing it wrong, but when I run multiple chains in parallel, it of course uses the parallel package to create a PSOCK cluster (why is this default, by the way? Why not use forking for unix systems?)

Sometimes I want to cancel the simulation, so I hit ctrl+c or the rstudio 'stop' icon. This does not stop the parallel cluster though, just further execution of the stan command. So I have to open top/htop and manually kill the parallel processes.

Is there any way to stop the cluster from R itself, just to improve the user experience?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] rstan Suggestion (Tip?): Cancelling mcmc
parts:
There's no way built in that I know. If anyone knows
a CRAN-compatible way we can do this, please let us know.
I'm reluctant to start writing things that kill processes
on client machines, no matter how good our intention, unless
we can be absolutely sure we're doing it safely.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] rstan Suggestion (Tip?): Cancelling mcmc
parts:
On Tuesday, November 29, 2016 at 5:00:36 PM UTC-5, Stephen Martin wrote:
Is there no callback method that could be used? Like, "on event user cancels, execute parallel::stopCluster(cl)" [commands not real, just giving concept].

There is a callback mechanism that works fine if you are doing R from a shell. The RStudio interface interferes with that somehow but we don't understand why. I think we will do forking on non-Windows in rstan 2.13.x but not from RStudio because then the user can't see the progress output.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] rstan Suggestion (Tip?): Cancelling mcmc
parts: Could a solution be to give rstan::sampling a "cluster" argument that defaults to Null but, if passed a parallel cluster object, uses that cluster instead of initializing one from scratch? That way, if the user hits stop in the gui, they can use parallel::stopCluster themselves on the cluster they created outside rstan::sampling.
